value.first: Six months is right on time, and the method I'd use is iron-first solids with early allergen introduction. Two clocks are running: his iron stores from birth are running low now, and waiting on allergens backfires - the LEAP trial found about 80% less peanut allergy in babies who ate peanut early and often instead of avoiding it. Day 1: upright in the high chair, a spoon or two of iron-fortified oat cereal, pureed beef, or mashed lentils. Most lands on the tray. That's a win.
value.second: Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, with mashed veg and fruit alongside. Milk or formula carries on as usual. Week 2, peanut first: in the morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter into warm water or a puree he knows (never a glob, never whole nuts). Tiny taste, wait 10 minutes, then feed the rest and keep him in sight two hours. Next day, well-cooked egg the same way, then one new allergen a day - yogurt, wheat, tofu, sesame, fish.
value.third: Once a food is tolerated keep it in about twice a week - dropping it can undo the protection. Lumpy and soft finger foods by 9 months. Gagging is noisy and normal; choking is silent. Refusal just means try again another day. If he has moderate-to-severe eczema, talk to your provider before the allergen run - guided, not delayed. Emma Hubbard, a paediatric OT, has a good starting-solids walkthrough. I'll check in Thursday.
